sanskrit: evam ukto vasiṣṭhena viśvāmitro mahābalaḥ āgneyam astram utkṣipya tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: Thus addressed by Vasiṣṭha, the mighty Viśvāmitra raised his fire-weapon and cried out, "Stand! Stand!"

sanskrit: vasiṣṭho bhagavān krodhād idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: The venerable Vasiṣṭha, in his anger, spoke these words:

sanskrit: kṣatrabandho sthito 'smy eṣa yad balaṃ tad vidarśaya nāśayāmy eṣa te darpaṃ śastrasya tava gādhija
english: "O wretch of a kṣatriya, here I stand — show whatever strength you possess! I shall destroy your pride in weapons, O son of Gādhi."

sanskrit: kva ca te kṣatriyabalaṃ kva ca brahmabalaṃ mahat paśya brahmabalaṃ divyaṃ mama kṣatriyapāṃsana
english: "Where is your kṣatriya strength, and where is the great power of brahman? Behold my divine power of brahman, O disgrace to the kṣatriyas!"

sanskrit: tasyāstraṃ gādhiputrasya ghoram āgneyam uttamam brahmadaṇḍena tac chāntam agner vega ivāmbhasā
english: That dreadful, supreme fire-weapon of the son of Gādhi was quenched by the brahma-staff, as the force of fire is quenched by water.

sanskrit: vāruṇaṃ caiva raudraṃ ca aindraṃ pāśupataṃ tathā aiṣīkaṃ cāpi cikṣepa ruṣito gādhinandanaḥ
english: In fury, the son of Gādhi then hurled the vāruṇa weapon, the raudra weapon, the āindra weapon, the pāśupata weapon, and also the aiṣīka weapon.

sanskrit: mānavaṃ mohanaṃ caiva gāndharvaṃ svāpanaṃ tathā jṛmbhaṇaṃ mohanaṃ caiva saṃtāpanavilāpane
english: He also discharged the mānava weapon, the mohana (bewildering) weapon, the gāndharvā weapon, the svāpana (stupefying) weapon, the jṛmbhaṇa (yawning) weapon, another mohana weapon, the saṃtāpana (tormenting) weapon, and the vilāpana (lamenting) weapon.

sanskrit: śoṣaṇaṃ dāraṇaṃ caiva vajram astraṃ sudurjayam brahmapāśaṃ kālapāśaṃ vāruṇaṃ pāśam eva ca
english: He hurled the śoṣaṇa (desiccating) weapon, the dāraṇa (rending) weapon, the vajra weapon most difficult to withstand, the brahma-noose, the kāla-noose, and the varuṇa-noose.

sanskrit: pinākāstraṃ ca dayitaṃ śuṣkārdre aśanī tathā daṇḍāstram atha paiśācaṃ krauñcam astraṃ tathaiva ca
english: He hurled the beloved pinākāstra, the two thunderbolts — the dry and the wet — the daṇḍa weapon, the paiśāca weapon, and likewise the krauñca weapon.

sanskrit: dharmacakraṃ kālacakraṃ viṣṇucakraṃ tathaiva ca vāyavyaṃ mathanaṃ caiva astraṃ hayaśiras tathā
english: He discharged the dharma-disc, the kāla-disc, and likewise the Viṣṇu-disc; the vāyavya (wind) weapon, the mathana (churning) weapon, and the hayaśiras (horse-head) weapon.

sanskrit: śaktidvayaṃ ca cikṣepa kaṅkālaṃ musalaṃ tathā vaidyādharaṃ mahāstraṃ ca kālāstram atha dāruṇam
english: He also hurled a pair of śakti missiles, the kaṅkāla (skeleton) weapon, the musala (mace) weapon, the great vaidyādhara weapon, and the terrible kāla weapon.

sanskrit: triśūlam astraṃ ghoraṃ ca kāpālam atha kaṅkaṇam etāny astrāṇi cikṣepa sarvāṇi raghunandana
english: He hurled the dreadful triśūla (trident) weapon, the kāpāla weapon, and the kaṅkaṇa weapon — all these weapons did he discharge, O joy of the Raghu line.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭhe japatāṃ śreṣṭhe tad adbhutam ivābhavat tāni sarvāṇi daṇḍena grasate brahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ
english: Against Vasiṣṭha, foremost among those who recite mantras, it was as though a marvel had occurred: the son of Brahman swallowed all those weapons with his staff.

sanskrit: teṣu śānteṣu brahmāstraṃ kṣiptavān gādhinandanaḥ tad astram udyataṃ dṛṣṭvā devāḥ sāgnipurogamāḥ
english: When all those were quelled, the son of Gādhi released the brahmāstra. Seeing that weapon raised, the gods led by Agni,

sanskrit: devarṣayaś ca saṃbhrāntā gandharvāḥ samahoragāḥ trailokyam āsīt saṃtrastaṃ brahmāstre samudīrite
english: the divine seers in agitation, and the gandharvas together with the great serpents — all three worlds were seized with terror when the brahmāstra was discharged.

sanskrit: tad apy astraṃ mahāghoraṃ brāhmaṃ brāhmeṇa tejasā vasiṣṭho grasate sarvaṃ brahmadaṇḍena rāghava
english: That also — that most dreadful brahma weapon — Vasiṣṭha swallowed entirely with his brahma-staff by the power of brahman, O Rāghava.

sanskrit: brahmāstraṃ grasamānasya vasiṣṭhasya mahātmanaḥ trailokyamohanaṃ raudraṃ rūpam āsīt sudāruṇam
english: As the great-souled Vasiṣṭha swallowed the brahmāstra, his form became exceedingly dreadful — bewildering to all three worlds and ferocious.

sanskrit: romakūpeṣu sarveṣu vasiṣṭhasya mahātmanaḥ marīcya iva niṣpetur agner dhūmākulārciṣaḥ
english: From all the pores of the great-souled Vasiṣṭha's body there burst forth flames like rays of fire, dense with smoke.

sanskrit: prājvalad brahmadaṇḍaś ca vasiṣṭhasya karodyataḥ vidhūma iva kālāgnir yamadaṇḍa ivāparaḥ
english: The brahma-staff raised in Vasiṣṭha's hand blazed like the smokeless fire of universal dissolution, or like a second staff of Yama.

sanskrit: tato 'stuvan munigaṇā vasiṣṭhaṃ japatāṃ varam amoghaṃ te balaṃ brahmaṃs tejo dhāraya tejasā
english: Then the assemblies of sages praised Vasiṣṭha, foremost among the reciters: "Your power is unfailing, O brahman — sustain your splendour with your splendour."

sanskrit: nigṛhītas tvayā brahman viśvāmitro mahātapāḥ prasīda japatāṃ śreṣṭha lokāḥ santu gatavyathāḥ
english: "The great ascetic Viśvāmitra has been subdued by you, O brahman. Be gracious, O foremost among chanters, and let the worlds be freed of their anguish."

sanskrit: evam ukto mahātejāḥ śamaṃ cakre mahātapāḥ viśvāmitro 'pi nikṛto viniḥśvasyedam abravīt
english: Thus addressed, the great-splendoured and great-ascetic Vasiṣṭha became calm. And Viśvāmitra, humiliated, breathed a deep sigh and spoke these words:

sanskrit: dhig balaṃ kṣatriyabalaṃ brahmatejobalaṃ balam ekena brahmadaṇḍena sarvāstrāṇi hatāni me
english: "Shame upon kṣatriya strength — the power of brahman's splendour is the true strength! All my weapons have been struck down by a single brahma-staff."

sanskrit: tad etat samavekṣyāhaṃ prasannendriyamānasaḥ tapo mahat samāsthāsye yad vai brahmatvakārakam
english: "Having thus reflected, with senses and mind at peace, I shall undertake great austerity — that which indeed brings about the state of brahmanhood."

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃtaptahṛdayaḥ smaran nigraham ātmanaḥ viniḥśvasya viniḥśvasya kṛtavairo mahātmanā
english: Then, with a burning heart, remembering his own defeat, sighing again and again, and bearing enmity toward the great-souled one,

sanskrit: sa dakṣiṇāṃ diśaṃ gatvā mahiṣyā saha rāghava tatāpa paramaṃ ghoraṃ viśvāmitro mahātapāḥ phalamūlāśano dāntaś cacāra paramaṃ tapaḥ
english: Viśvāmitra, that great ascetic, went to the southern quarter along with his chief wife, O Rāghava, and performed the most intense and dreadful austerity; subsisting on fruits and roots, self-restrained, he practised supreme tapas.

sanskrit: athāsya jajñire putrāḥ satyadharmaparāyaṇāḥ haviṣpando madhuṣpando dṛḍhanetro mahārathaḥ
english: Then there were born to him sons devoted to truth and righteousness: Haviṣpanda, Madhuṣpanda, Dṛḍhanetra, and Mahāratha.

sanskrit: pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ abravīn madhuraṃ vākyaṃ viśvāmitraṃ tapodhanam
english: When a full thousand years had elapsed, Brahmā, the grandsire of the worlds, spoke sweetly to Viśvāmitra, the treasury of austerity:

sanskrit: jitā rājarṣilokās te tapasā kuśikātmaja anena tapasā tvāṃ hi rājarṣir iti vidmahe
english: "The worlds of the royal seers have been won by you through your austerity, O son of Kuśika. By this austerity we recognise you as a royal seer (rājarṣi)."

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahātejā jagāma saha daivataiḥ triviṣṭapaṃ brahmalokaṃ lokānāṃ parameśvaraḥ
english: Having spoken thus, that great-splendoured supreme lord of the worlds departed with the gods to the triple heaven, the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: viśvāmitro 'pi tac chrutvā hriyā kiṃ cid avāṅmukhaḥ duḥkhena mahatāviṣṭaḥ samanyur idam abravīt
english: Viśvāmitra, hearing this, hung his head slightly in shame, overcome by great sorrow, and spoke with indignation:

sanskrit: tapaś ca sumahat taptaṃ rājarṣir iti māṃ viduḥ devāḥ sarṣigaṇāḥ sarve nāsti manye tapaḥphalam
english: "I have undergone very great austerity, yet the gods with all the assemblies of sages know me only as a royal seer. I think the fruit of my austerity is nothing."

sanskrit: evaṃ niścitya manasā bhūya eva mahātapāḥ tapaś cacāra kākutstha paramaṃ paramātmavān
english: Having thus resolved in his mind, the great ascetic, of supreme self-mastery, once more performed supreme austerity, O scion of Kākutstha.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu satyavādī jitendriyaḥ triśaṅkur iti vikhyāta ikṣvāku kulanandanaḥ
english: At this very time, a truth-speaking, sense-conquering descendant of the Ikṣvāku lineage, known by the name Triśaṅku,

sanskrit: tasya buddhiḥ samutpannā yajeyam iti rāghava gaccheyaṃ svaśarīreṇa devānāṃ paramāṃ gatim
english: had a resolve arise in his mind, O Rāghava: "I shall perform a sacrifice and reach the highest abode of the gods in my own body."

sanskrit: sa vasiṣṭhaṃ samāhūya kathayām āsa cintitam aśakyam iti cāpy ukto vasiṣṭhena mahātmanā
english: He summoned Vasiṣṭha and told him his thought; but the great-souled Vasiṣṭha told him it was impossible.

sanskrit: pratyākhyāto vasiṣṭhena sa yayau dakṣiṇāṃ diśam vasiṣṭhā dīrgha tapasas tapo yatra hi tepire
english: Refused by Vasiṣṭha, he went to the southern quarter, to the place where the sons of Vasiṣṭha were performing their long austerities.

sanskrit: triśaṅkuḥ sumahātejāḥ śataṃ paramabhāsvaram vasiṣṭhaputrān dadṛśe tapyamānān yaśasvinaḥ
english: The greatly splendoured Triśaṅku beheld the hundred glorious sons of Vasiṣṭha, resplendent in the highest degree, engaged in their austerities.

sanskrit: so 'bhigamya mahātmānaḥ sarvān eva guroḥ sutān abhivādyānupūrvyeṇa hriyā kiṃ cid avāṅmukhaḥ abravīt sumahātejāḥ sarvān eva kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: Approaching them, those great-souled sons of his teacher, he saluted them in proper order and, hanging his head somewhat in shame, the greatly splendoured one addressed them all with joined palms.

sanskrit: śaraṇaṃ vaḥ prapadye 'haṃ śaraṇyāñ śaraṇāgataḥ pratyākhyāto 'smi bhadraṃ vo vasiṣṭhena mahātmanā
english: "I take refuge in you, O worthy refuge, as one who has come for shelter. Good fortune to you — I have been refused by the great-souled Vasiṣṭha."

sanskrit: yaṣṭukāmo mahāyajñaṃ tad anujñātum arthatha guruputrān ahaṃ sarvān namaskṛtya prasādaye
english: "Wishing to perform a great sacrifice, I seek your permission for that. Bowing to all of you, sons of my teacher, I entreat your grace."

sanskrit: śirasā praṇato yāce brāhmaṇāṃs tapasi sthitān te māṃ bhavantaḥ siddhyarthaṃ yājayantu samāhitāḥ saśarīro yathāhaṃ hi devalokam avāpnuyām
english: "Bowing with my head, I beseech the brāhmaṇas established in austerity: let your honours, with concentration, officiate my sacrifice for its fulfillment, so that I may attain the world of the gods in my own body."

sanskrit: pratyākhyāto vasiṣṭhena gatim anyāṃ tapodhanāḥ guruputrān ṛte sarvān nāhaṃ paśyāmi kāṃ cana
english: "Refused by Vasiṣṭha, O treasuries of austerity, I see no other recourse whatsoever except all of you, the sons of my teacher."

sanskrit: ikṣvākūṇāṃ hi sarveṣāṃ purodhāḥ paramā gatiḥ tasmād anantaraṃ sarve bhavanto daivataṃ mama
english: "The family priest is the highest resort for all the Ikṣvākus; therefore, next after him, all of you are my divinities."

sanskrit: tatas triśaṅkor vacanaṃ śrutvā krodhasamanvitam ṛṣiputraśataṃ rāma rājānam idam abravīt
english: Then, having heard Triśaṅku's speech filled with anger, the hundred sons of the sage, O Rāma, spoke thus to the king:

sanskrit: pratyākhyāto 'si durbuddhe guruṇā satyavādinā taṃ kathaṃ samatikramya śākhāntaram upeyivān
english: "You have been refused, O foolish one, by the teacher who speaks only truth — how can you, having bypassed him, have come to a different branch?"

sanskrit: ikṣvākūṇāṃ hi sarveṣāṃ purodhāḥ paramā gatiḥ na cātikramituṃ śakyaṃ vacanaṃ satyavādinaḥ
english: "The family priest is the highest resort for all the Ikṣvākus; it is not possible to transgress the word of the truth-speaker."

sanskrit: aśakyam iti covāca vasiṣṭho bhagavān ṛṣiḥ taṃ vayaṃ vai samāhartuṃ kratuṃ śaktāḥ kathaṃ tava
english: "The venerable sage Vasiṣṭha has declared it impossible — how then are we capable of performing that sacrifice for you?"

sanskrit: bāliśas tvaṃ naraśreṣṭha gamyatāṃ svapuraṃ punaḥ yājane bhagavāñ śaktas trailokyasyāpi pārthiva
english: "You are foolish, O best of men — return to your own city. The venerable one is capable of officiating for even the three worlds, O king."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā krodhaparyākulākṣaram sa rājā punar evaitān idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Hearing their speech, agitated by anger, the king spoke again to them these words:

sanskrit: pratyākhyāto 'smi guruṇā guruputrais tathaiva ca anyāṃ gatiṃ gamiṣyāmi svasti vo 'stu tapodhanāḥ
english: "I have been refused by my teacher and likewise by the sons of my teacher; I shall seek another recourse. Good fortune be with you, O treasuries of austerity."

sanskrit: ṛṣiputrās tu tac chrutvā vākyaṃ ghorābhisaṃhitam śepuḥ paramasaṃkruddhāś caṇḍālatvaṃ gamiṣyasi evam uktvā mahātmāno viviśus te svam āśramam
english: But the sons of the sage, hearing that speech laden with dreadful intent, cursed him in supreme wrath: "You shall become a caṇḍāla!" Having spoken thus, those great-souled ones entered their own hermitage.

sanskrit: atha rātryāṃ vyatītāyāṃ rājā caṇḍālatāṃ gataḥ nīlavastradharo nīlaḥ paruṣo dhvastamūrdhajaḥ cityamālyānulepaś ca āyasābharaṇo 'bhavat
english: Then, when the night had passed, the king had become a caṇḍāla: wearing dark garments, dark in complexion, rough, with hair dishevelled, wearing garlands and unguents from funeral pyres, and adorned with iron ornaments.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā mantriṇaḥ sarve tyaktvā caṇḍālarūpiṇam prādravan sahitā rāma paurā ye 'syānugāminaḥ
english: Seeing him transformed into the form of a caṇḍāla, all his ministers and the townspeople who were his followers fled together, O Rāma.

sanskrit: eko hi rājā kākutstha jagāma paramātmavān dahyamāno divārātraṃ viśvāmitraṃ tapodhanam
english: Alone, that king of supreme self-possession, O scion of Kākutstha, burning day and night in anguish, went to Viśvāmitra, the treasury of austerity.

sanskrit: viśvāmitras tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā rājānaṃ viphalīkṛtam caṇḍālarūpiṇaṃ rāma muniḥ kāruṇyam āgataḥ
english: Viśvāmitra, seeing that king reduced to failure, in the form of a caṇḍāla, O Rāma, was moved to compassion.

sanskrit: kāruṇyāt sa mahātejā vākyaṃ parama dhārmikaḥ idaṃ jagāda bhadraṃ te rājānaṃ ghoradarśanam
english: Out of compassion, that greatly splendoured and supremely righteous one spoke these words, wishing him well, to the king of dreadful appearance:

sanskrit: kim āgamanakāryaṃ te rājaputra mahābala ayodhyādhipate vīra śāpāc caṇḍālatāṃ gataḥ
english: "What is the purpose of your coming, O prince, O mighty one, O hero, lord of Ayodhyā — you who have been reduced to caṇḍāla-hood by a curse?"

sanskrit: atha tad vākyam ākarṇya rājā caṇḍālatāṃ gataḥ abravīt prāñjalir vākyaṃ vākyajño vākyakovidam
english: Then, hearing those words, the king who had attained caṇḍāla-hood, skilled in speech, spoke with joined palms to the one expert in speech:

sanskrit: pratyākhyāto 'smi guruṇā guruputrais tathaiva ca anavāpyaiva taṃ kāmaṃ mayā prāpto viparyayaḥ
english: "I have been refused by my teacher and likewise by the sons of my teacher; without having attained that desire of mine, I have met with this calamity."

sanskrit: saśarīro divaṃ yāyām iti me saumyadarśanam mayā ceṣṭaṃ kratuśataṃ tac ca nāvāpyate phalam
english: "It was my gentle-visaged wish to ascend to heaven in my own body; I have striven with a hundred sacrifices, yet that fruit is not obtained."

sanskrit: anṛtaṃ nokta pūrvaṃ me na ca vakṣye kadā cana kṛcchreṣv api gataḥ saumya kṣatradharmeṇa te śape
english: "I have never spoken untruth in the past, nor shall I ever speak it — even gone into hardships, O gentle one, I swear to you by the dharma of the kṣatriya."

sanskrit: yajñair bahuvidhair iṣṭaṃ prajā dharmeṇa pālitāḥ guravaś ca mahātmānaḥ śīlavṛttena toṣitāḥ
english: "I have made offerings with many and various sacrifices; my subjects have been protected by righteousness; the great-souled teachers have been gratified by conduct and good character."

sanskrit: dharme prayatamānasya yajñaṃ cāhartum icchataḥ paritoṣaṃ na gacchanti guravo munipuṃgava
english: "Though I strive in righteousness and wish to perform sacrifice, the teachers are not pleased — O foremost of sages."

sanskrit: daivam eva paraṃ manye pauruṣaṃ tu nirarthakam daivenākramyate sarvaṃ daivaṃ hi paramā gatiḥ
english: "I hold fate alone to be supreme; human effort is futile. Everything is overridden by fate, for fate is the highest resort."

sanskrit: tasya me paramārtasya prasādam abhikāṅkṣataḥ kartum arhasi bhadraṃ te daivopahatakarmaṇaḥ
english: "For me, thus deeply afflicted and seeking your grace, O one of good fortune, whose actions have been undone by fate — you should show your favour."

sanskrit: nānyāṃ gatiṃ gamiṣyāmi nānyaḥ śaraṇam asti me daivaṃ puruṣakāreṇa nivartayitum arhasi
english: "I shall seek no other recourse; there is no other refuge for me. You should turn back fate by the power of human effort."
